box: Crash/fault tests at every durable transition and concurrent remote edits (milestone 2)
method: Enumerated the journal modules containing fsync or transaction commits, then read the tests that reach each. Test names were not used as evidence; see docs/development.md on why that undercounts here.

rows.note: Kills the process mid-queue and asserts pending, uncertain and acknowledged records each survive in their own state.
SIGKILL between a sealed save and later unsealed writes; the fsynced payload survives verbatim and the newer bytes stay readable.
SIGKILL around a mutation; a pending outcome and an acknowledged receipt both survive.
No kill point. tests/upload_preparation.rs covers rollback and interrupted preparation by injection, not by process death.
Reached only indirectly; no test kills between a generation advance and its commit.

tests/clean_handoff.rs asserts a failed detach transaction keeps its rows, bytes and cleanup intents together, and that restart finishes only explicit cleanup -- injected failure and restart, not process death mid-commit.
Replacement has three kernel fixtures; none kills the process mid-commit.
tests/unlinked_files.rs covers rollback by injection; no kill point.
tests/local_directories.rs covers restart; no kill mid-commit.

conclusion: Four of eleven journal modules carrying durable transitions have a test that kills the process at one. The other seven are covered for rollback and restart by injected failure, which is narrower evidence: an injected error unwinds a transaction the program still controls, while a SIGKILL leaves whatever the kernel had actually written. The box says every transition, and seven are not that. It stays unticked.
cheapest_next_step: The subprocess pattern already exists four times over -- re-exec the test binary with --exact <fixture> --ignored, a ready sentinel and a Drop guard. Adding a kill point per module is mechanical rather than novel; preparation, handoff and replacements are the three whose commits span the most state and are worth doing first.
not_reachable_autonomously: Physical power loss and a lying fsync are a different class again, need dm-flakey and root, and the milestone text already names physical-fault coverage as an open gap.
